question: Cognizant Digital Nurture 5.0 final interview. The OOP discussion covered all the OOP concepts with real-life examples, then **polymorphism** (compile-time and runtime). The candidate happened to mention annotations, which led to: **what is an annotation**, give some examples (the candidate named `SuppressWarnings` and `FunctionalInterface`), **what is a functional interface**, and finally "if you can create an interface, can you do it for us": the candidate had to **write their own functional interface in the interviewer's online editor and use it**. The candidate managed this only partially.
lookingFor: Solid Java fundamentals: annotations, interfaces, lambdas.
Ability to write short, correct code live in an unfamiliar editor.
Understanding of why functional interfaces exist (lambdas, streams).
Link between OOP concepts and modern Java features.
followUps: Can a functional interface have default methods? Why?
What is the difference between a lambda and an anonymous inner class?
What are @Retention and @Target on a custom annotation?
Name the main java.util.function interfaces and when you would use each.
